transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Vanguard VP Eng), Carlos (Platform Lead), Tina (Security Dir), Samir (SRE)

Summary:
Initial discovery focused on high-availability expectations for patient-facing LLM endpoints, multi-region routing, and fallback behavior during partial outages. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for PHI workloads; strong emphasis on auditability and KMS. Agreed POC to validate multi-region failover and degraded-mode responses.

Topics:
- Current infra and traffic profile
- SLA targets and acceptable degradations
- Fallback policies (cached responses, model downgrade, regional failover)
- Security/compliance (HIPAA, KMS, audit logs)
- POC scope and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: all right everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Hayes from Redwood Inference, I'm joined by Priya and Ethan, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, just want to understand your resilience constraints and what success looks like for you, Maya do you want to kick off with why you reached out?
[00:17] Maya: sure yeah hey everybody, thanks. Vanguard built a patient intake assistant and we're pushing it into production next quarter, main concerns are latency for live chat and risk profile for PHI, also we need a plan if a whole region goes down or API spikes, so we're evaluating if Redwood hosted is safe or if we must go Dedicated or Private.
[00:34] Carlos: to add, our traffic is pretty spiky - clinic hours see a hard ramp, p95 right now is about 420ms for our current microservices, for LLM calls we'd like p95 < 800ms ideally and SLO 99.95 for the critical flow.
[00:52] Priya: got it, thanks. quick clarification - when you say 99.95, is that target for user-facing token latency or for end-to-end request that includes any upstream transforms?
[01:05] Maya: end-to-end, so from user click to final reply. We can tolerate some graceful degradation if it's defined - e.g., shorter answer or cached reply during failover is ok, just not blackouts.
[01:20] Samir: and security wise, everything touching PHI must stay inside our VPC and go through our KMS; we need audit logs and proof of key access controls.
[01:30] Jordan: that's totally reasonable. high level, there are three modes you mentioned: Hosted (our managed API), Dedicated (reserved gpu pools for you), and Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted is fastest to go live, supports multi-region routing and fallback, but doesn't give you tenant-level dedicated hardware. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and stronger isolation and SLA options. Private gives the most control for PHI but takes longer to deploy.
[01:55] Ethan: one nuance I want to highlight - for multi-region failover we have two patterns: active-active routing with smart request routing by latency and health, or active-passive with warm standbys. both have tradeoffs for cold-start times and cost.
[02:12] Carlos: can you do active-active with consistent KV cache? our model uses prefix caching for patient context, we can't lose that state.
[02:25] Priya: yes, we have options. we replicate the KV cache across regions asynchronously for most workloads; for strict consistency we recommend session-affinity or routing by region with prefix caching and a short TTL. the word on the docs is "KV cache" but sometimes the auto-transcriber prints "kayvee cache" so i apologize for the noise.
[02:43] Tina: on the compliance front, can Redwood support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and provide tamper-evident audit logs? we need to show this to our legal team.
[02:58] Jordan: yes. we support bringing your own KMS key for encryption at rest, and we can integrate with HSM providers. audit logs are part of our enterprise package - they include per-request metadata with model version, route, token usage.
[03:15] Maya: what about SLA language - specifically, if the primary region fails and we lose a percent of traffic, what's the commitment?
[03:25] Ethan: our standard hosted SLA is 99.9 for availability for standard customers; enterprise Dedicated can be negotiated to 99.95 with reserved capacity and runbooks. important detail: when a region is down we provide automated routing to other regions, but availability depends on whether a compatible model variant is warm in the fallback region.
[03:45] Samir: so if the fallback region only has a quantized 4-bit variant, will responses be different? could that break downstream logic or hallucinate more?
[03:55] Priya: good question. model variant changes can affect output distribution. we recommend a couple of strategies: 1) keep a warm, same-architecture replica with identical weights across regions for exact parity, 2) if cost prohibits that, fall back to a smaller/quantized variant but gate key outputs through a regeneration or confidence check, 3) static cached answers for the most common prompts as an emergency mode.
[04:20] Carlos: what's the warm-up time if you need to spin a model in the other region?
[04:26] Ethan: depends on model size and whether we have pre-pulled weights. for an Llama-variant ~13B, warm start from cold can be 30-90s; with pre-warmed containers and KV in memory, we can be <10s for first token, but that costs reserved capacity.
[04:40] Maya: 30-90s might be too long for the clinical triage flow, users might think it's down. we prefer behavior that returns something in <2s even under degradation.
[04:50] Priya: that's where degraded-mode responses come in - for critical API endpoints we can enable a "fallback mode" that returns short deterministic responses from a cached store or template within 200-500ms, while async regeneration to the best-effort model happens in the background.
[05:06] Samir: how do you measure and report these degradations? we need visibility to correlate incidents.
[05:12] Jordan: Console provides per-route SLO graphs, token-level latency breakdown, and an incident timeline. we push traces and SLO breach alerts to your pager. you can configure alerting on percent degraded responses too.
[05:27] Tina: auditability - will logs include whether a response was served from cache versus model? we need that for forensics.
[05:35] Priya: yes logs annotate source: model, cache, fallback-template, quantized-variant and include model-version/hash. there are some transcribe mislabels sometimes but the data is there.
[05:47] Maya: tell us about network failover - we run primarily in GCP us-east, are you able to route to us-west or AWS if GCP is down?
[05:57] Ethan: yep, multi-cloud routing is supported; we typically host in multiple clouds or regions, and routing policy can be latency-based, cost-based, or forced by policy (eg regulatory residency). we can also do a geographic hierarchy so EU traffic remains in EU unless there's a full-region outage.
[06:15] Carlos: any constraints with private deployments? if we go Private (VPC), how do you handle multi-region? do you need a separate private instance per region?
[06:26] Priya: Private generally means we deploy a customer-specific control plane and optionally data plane into your VPC. for multi-region you'd either replicate the data plane into both regions or use secure cross-region networking. replication increases complexity but gives fastest failover. there's also a hybrid option where control plane is private and we use Redwood-managed model replicas across regions.
[06:45] Samir: curious about cost math - reserved capacity in two regions seems expensive. is there a recommended cheap fallback pattern?
[06:53] Jordan: common pattern is reserved capacity in primary region + smaller reserved or on-demand warm in a hot-standby region, and a cached/responses emergency tier that avoids model compute for the most critical flows. Redwood Optimize also suggests batching and quantization policies that reduce per-token cost.
[07:10] Tina: our legal will want to see language around rollback and change control - e.g., if a model update causes a regression, we need a canary and the ability to automatically rollback to previous commit.
[07:22] Priya: we support canary rollouts and automatic rollback on regression criteria. you can tie rollout gating to evals and prompt sets.
[07:30] Maya: you mentioned telemetry - can we get request traces with patient-id redaction? we can't send PHI to Redwood without encryption and contract, but we need enough telemetry to debug.
[07:40] Jordan: redaction is supported. we can accept hashed or pseudonymized IDs and keep metadata like token counts and latency. full PHI in payloads is only permitted in Private deployments or under Business Associate Agreement - we'll include that in the docs.
[07:58] Samir: let's discuss an outage scenario: regional availability zone goes offline, network partition - what happens to in-flight sessions and user tokens?
[08:08] Ethan: for in-flight sessions we checkpoint the KV cache periodically; on partition we'll route new requests to the healthy region and surface a degraded flag to clients. clients can retry with idempotency keys. we recommend short checkpoint intervals for critical sessions.
[08:24] Carlos: checkpoint frequency increases overhead, any suggestions for tradeoff?
[08:28] Priya: yes, it's a balance - typical windows are 5-30s depending on tolerance. for triage flows we suggest 5s checkpoints. Also prefix caching can help reduce need to reconstruct full context.
[08:40] Maya: are there constraints around model versions in fallbacks? if we have a pinned version can Redwood preserve that across regions?
[08:48] Jordan: absolutely; you can pin model versions per-route and pin rollout policies. pinned versions are included in the Dedicated SLA.
[08:55] Tina: on encryption, we need to ensure keys never leave our control - does Redwood support KMS requests proxied through customer KMS?
[09:02] Ethan: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported. we can integrate with your cloud KMS or HSM and keys can remain under your control. we'll surface key usage metrics without exposing key material.
[09:14] Maya: what's the POC you would propose to validate these claims?
[09:20] Priya: propose a 4-week POC: week 1 - architecture & config (define routes, pinned models, keys), week 2 - deploy in two regions with warm standby and KV replication, week 3 - run failover drills (simulated region outage, network partition), week 4 - analysis and handoff with SLO reports. we'll instrument the console to show degraded responses, cache hit ratios, and p95/p99.
[09:45] Carlos: can you share a bench spreadsheet that shows token cost under active-active vs standby + cached fallback?
[09:52] Jordan: yes we'll send a template. it will include assumptions like QPS, model size, avg tokens per call, and expected cost delta for replication.
[09:59] Samir: what about edge cases like third-party integrations timing out - does Redwood provide request-level timeouts/backpressure hooks?
[10:07] Priya: there are request timeouts, retry middleware, and client-side backpressure recommendations. you can configure hard timeouts per-route and a fallback policy called "best-effort then cached".
[10:20] Maya: any gotchas we should be aware of if we start with Hosted then move to Dedicated later?
[10:28] Jordan: main things are capacity planning and model pinning. Hosted is great for iteration; Dedicated requires capacity commitments but gives stronger SLOs and isolation. migration is supported and we keep the same API surface so app changes are minimal, but you will need a short maintenance window to switch traffic.
[10:42] Tina: timeline question - how long to stand up Dedicated with two regions?
[10:47] Ethan: typical is 4-6 weeks if models are in the catalog; if you need a custom model onboarding and private networking, plan 8-12 weeks.
[10:57] Maya: can you demo the console telemetry during the POC?
[11:00] Priya: yes we'll include console access scoped to read-only for your SREs and a playbook for incident runbook steps.
[11:10] Jordan: quick note on degradation UX - we recommend client-side indicators so users know they're in fallback mode, and server responses include a meta flag so app can display a notice.
[11:20] Samir: ok that's good. any live examples of customers who ran the failover drills?
[11:27] Priya: we had a healthcare customer run a full-region failover test last quarter and they sustained 98% of traffic with cached fallbacks for 2% of the most complex prompts; that was done on Dedicated with warm standbys.
[11:40] Carlos: great, what would you need from us to start the POC?
[11:44] Priya: sample traffic profile (QPS by endpoint), top 50 prompt templates, compliance checklist, and a contact for networking so we can design VPC peering if needed.
[11:55] Maya: we'll compile that. one last thing: do you have automatic degradation thresholds that we can tune? e.g., if latency > 1s, switch to cached answers for that route.
[12:03] Jordan: yes those policies are configurable per-route: latency thresholds, error thresholds, or percent degraded. we'll include recommended defaults.
[12:12] Tina: legal will want model audit trails - we may ask for probability/confidence metadata for outputs for high-risk flows.
[12:20] Priya: we can emit model confidence heuristics and token-level log snippets (with PHI redacted or pseudonymized for hosted). for Private, full logs can be retained according to your retention policy.
[12:34] Jordan: ok time check - we've got about 35 minutes covered, lots to action. to wrap, quick recap and next steps?
[12:41] Maya: recap from Vanguard: we want a POC to validate multi-region failover with degraded-mode responses under 2s, support for customer KMS, and an SLA around 99.95 for critical route.
[12:53] Jordan: Redwood will: 1) send SOC2+HIPAA docs and KMS integration notes, 2) send POC plan and bench spreadsheet, 3) propose timeline and pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated including a 2-region warm-standby option.
[13:06] Priya: action items same as in notes - I'll prepare the POC config and test plan.
[13:12] Carlos: we'll pull traffic profile and prompts and get them over this week.
[13:18] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll review the docs once received and loop legal on the BAA.
[13:23] Jordan: great, we'll follow up in the CRM and schedule the POC kickoff for the week of Mar 16, 2026. thanks all.

Notes / Observations (auto-generated):
- Customer strongly prefers deterministic, <2s degraded responses for critical flows.
- Budget sensitivity around reserved capacity; likely tradeoff: Dedicated primary + smaller standby or hybrid private-control-plane.
- Security gating points (KMS, BAA) will drive final deployment choice.
- Recommend POC that exercises region failover, cache hit ratios, and model parity checks.
